how_to_mine: Follow this plan exactly. Each lens agent reads only its pages (all are in the corpus; read them with `show <source_id> --around TEXT` or `--lines A:B`, tables with `tables <source_id>`), answers its demand items, and records each item as filled (fact ids), contradicted (what the page says instead) or not-found (where you looked). Never fetch a page that is already in the corpus and never pass --revalidate: a refresh changes snapshots that verified facts of other chapters quote (RULINGS 2026-10-14). Fetch a missing page only when a demand item needs it and no listed page answers it.

Write facts in files of 10 to 25 facts: _build/work/35-analytics/facts-<lens>-NN.json (lens file names: numbers, behavior, faq), then `facts add --file <that file> --by mine-35-<lens>`. Table rows and value lines: prefer `facts adopt` (--table/--row, --sentence, --heading). Every quote is copied verbatim from the page snapshot (.txt), never from full.md (full.md hits are pointers) and never from memory.

Each quote must carry every clause, scope, condition and exception of the claim on its own. When the condition stands in the next sentence (for example the Athena sentence 'You can request an increase in this timeout up to a maximum of 240 minutes.' belongs with the DML query timeout line, or 'although Athena supports querying AWS Glue tables that have 10 million partitions, Athena cannot read more than 1 million partitions in a single scan'), include that sentence in the quote; otherwise narrow the claim. Entail votes run on Opus and mark a clause found only in the surrounding text as partial.

Fact service keys: `athena` (ids start with `athena-`), `glue` (`glue-`), `lake-formation` (`lake-formation-`), `emr` (`emr-`; EMR Serverless and EMR on EKS facts too), `opensearch` (`opensearch-`), `quick` (`quick-`), `data-exchange` (`data-exchange-`). Decision-guide, whitepaper and Analytics Lens facts go under the service they describe; a general data-lake pattern fact goes under `lake-formation` when it is about governance and under `athena` when it is about querying in place; a format-and-partitioning best practice goes under `athena`. Neighbour facts: S3 `s3` (chapter 21), Data Firehose `data-firehose` and Kinesis `kinesis-data-streams` (chapter 34), Aurora `aurora` (27), RDS `rds` (26), DynamoDB `dynamodb` (28), Redshift `redshift` (chapter 30, not mined yet). Add a neighbour fact only after `facts list --service <key>` shows no fact that already answers it; reuse the existing id in the demand record when one exists (brief sources.neighbour_facts_to_reuse lists the known ones; n-rds.txt and n-aurora.txt list RDS and Aurora facts). A Redshift fact needed for the d056 comparison (for example what Redshift Spectrum does) may be added under `redshift` from docs/redshift/latest/dg/c-using-spectrum.

Every hard fact (number, limit, default, price, date, can/cannot, only/always/never) carries `question` (the demand question it answers) and at least two displays for kinds behavior, capability, restriction and default (brief gate B12). A display of a number-free fact is a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words from its quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11).

Names: write claims with the current names: Amazon Quick (its BI part is Amazon Quick Sight), Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon SageMaker AI, IAM Identity Center. Where a quote says 'QuickSight', 'Quick Suite', 'Elasticsearch Service' or 'Kinesis Data Firehose', keep the quote as it is; the writer handles 'formerly'. Glue 'primary' vs 'master' node: EMR pages say 'primary node'; quote as written.

Scope matters here: Athena numbers differ by Region (active DML queries) and by engine; Glue minimum billing durations differ by Glue version and job type (Spark, streaming, Python shell, Ray); EMR limits differ for instance fleets vs instance groups and console vs API; OpenSearch limits differ by instance type and by managed domain vs Serverless; Quick limits differ by edition or plan and by SPICE vs direct query. Put the scope in the claim and make sure the quote states it.

Changes: a fact touched by a change item sets `changed` (date, old value only if a saved page states it verbatim) and `change_items`. A feature GA after 2026-07-15 gets the note `not examinable yet`: Glue 6.0 and its 30% price reduction (2026-08-12/21), Glue Data Quality free ETL anomaly detection (2026-08-05), OpenSearch Serverless 10,000 collections per group (2026-08-10), Amazon Quick Max (2026-09-03), Quick desktop GA (2026-09-09), EMR Long Term Support with Spark 4.1 (2026-09-22), EMR 7.14 (2026-09-22). Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only.

Case-study facts have kind `case-study` and a quote of at most 25 words. Only the ten usable case studies of brief sources.usable_case_studies; the eight in fetch_failures are the generic listing page.

numbers+changes.job: Every number, limit, default and price for Athena, Glue, Lake Formation, EMR, OpenSearch Service, Quick and Data Exchange: the quota pages first (Athena service-limits and General Reference table; Glue General Reference and troubleshooting-service-limits; Lake Formation General Reference; EMR quotas page and General Reference; OpenSearch limits; Quick data-source-limits; Data Exchange limits), then the numeric guide pages (Glue worker types and DPU, job timeout; Athena CTAS 100-partition limit and capacity reservations; EMR fleet and group limits, multiple primary nodes, HDFS replication; OpenSearch snapshots and Multi-AZ with Standby; SPICE limits), then the seven pricing pages (dimensions and units; prefer dimension facts over Regional dollar prices) and the four SLA pages. Then one change fact per change item listed in d018 to d023, with the date from the history row or the change-feed row (What's New pages fetched for 2025 and 2026 only), and a pointer to the current-truth fact. Kinds: limit, quota, default, price, pricing-dimension, change.
watch: Athena quota lines live in a bullet list on service-limits (not a table); the numbers per Region are in the General Reference table docs/general/latest/gr/athena. Adopt the table row with its header so 'Default' and 'Adjustable' stay in the quote; say in the claim which Region the value is for when the row names Regions.
Athena 240 minutes is the maximum a DML timeout can be raised to, not the default: quote the bullet that says so whole. 262144 bytes is 'not an adjustable quota': keep that clause.

Athena pricing: the 10 MB minimum and rounding, and the statement about failed or canceled queries, must come from the pricing page or the FAQ answer as written. Do not write 'DDL is free' unless a page says it.

Glue: billing minimums differ (for example a 1-minute minimum for Glue version 2.0 and later Spark jobs vs other job types); keep the version and job type in the claim. DPU definition (vCPU, GB) must be quoted from worker-types or the pricing page. The Glue 6.0 price reduction is not examinable yet; current prices on the pricing page may already include it: say which version a price applies to.

Glue for Ray: the history row of 2026-03-31 announces 'no longer open to new customers starting April 30, 2026'; the row of 2026-04-30 and awsglue-ray-jobs-availability-change give the current state. One change fact, dated, and one current-truth fact.

Lake Formation pricing: say exactly what is charged (the pricing page may list charges for storage optimization, data filtering requests or the Lake Formation APIs) and quote 'no additional charge' wording only as written. Governed Tables shutdown comes from full_shutdown_services with its date.

EMR fleets: the limit on instance types per fleet differs between the console and the API/CLI; keep both in one quote or narrow the claim. Multiple primary nodes need a minimum release: keep the release in the claim.
OpenSearch quotas are per instance type in long tables: adopt only the rows the demand names (domains per Region, instances per domain, UltraWarm); do not adopt per-instance EBS rows in bulk.

Quick: plan names and prices changed in 2026 (Free and Plus 2026-04-28); take current plan names from the pricing page and the FAQ, the date from the What's New page. SPICE limits: quote the row or sentence for the edition it applies to (Enterprise vs Standard).

What's New pages from 2020 to 2024 are disallowed by robots.txt (brief not_fetched_by_rule): for 2022-2024 changes use the change-feed row (changes for <service>) or the doc-history row, never memory.
SLA pages: quote the commitment sentence with its percentage and its scope (for example Multi-AZ with Standby domains vs other domains for OpenSearch).

behavior+decisions.job: Every behaviour, capability, restriction and decision rule the exam uses: Athena (what it is, tables and the Data Catalog, formats, columnar/compression/partitioning, partition projection, CTAS/INSERT INTO/UNLOAD for format conversion, query results and encryption, workgroups and data usage controls, federated query, service logs, security and cross-account access, Lake Formation enforcement, Glacier restore, capacity reservations, Spark, Iceberg); Glue (components, Data Catalog, crawlers, ETL jobs and format conversion, Relationalize, job bookmarks, triggers and workflows, streaming ETL, Flex, sensitive data detection, Data Quality, data preparation, security configurations and VPC connections, zero-ETL, Schema Registry); Lake Formation (what it is, permission model with IAM, registered locations and credential vending, default settings and hybrid access mode, fine-grained column/row/cell security with data filters, LF-TBAC, cross-account sharing and resource links, audit, blueprints); EMR (what it is, deployment options, node types, single-AZ and multiple primary nodes, HDFS vs EMRFS, transient vs long-running, auto-termination, purchasing options and Spot guidance, fleets vs groups, managed scaling, EMR Serverless, security); service cards OpenSearch, Quick, Data Exchange; the decision guide, whitepapers and Analytics Lens; the comparisons Athena vs Redshift vs EMR vs Glue, the CSV-to-Parquet paths; the Callvale decision facts (d060 lists the reasons); one or two case studies. Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, default, decision, case-study.
watch: Athena 'serverless' and 'no infrastructure to manage' claims need the what-is sentence as written; 'pay only for the queries you run' needs the page or FAQ sentence. Do not write 'Athena replaces S3 Select' unless a saved page says it; the S3 Select closure itself is the reused s3 fact.

Tables are metadata: a claim that dropping an Athena table leaves the S3 data needs a sentence that says so (search 'DROP TABLE' in the corpus, docs/athena/latest/ug/drop-table is not in the corpus: fetch it only if no listed page states it).
Workgroup data usage controls: the per-query limit cancels a query that exceeds it; the per-workgroup limit raises an alarm or action. Keep the two apart and quote each with its condition.

Lake Formation defaults (d042): new databases and tables have IAMAllowedPrincipals / 'Use only IAM access control' unless the setting is changed; quote change-settings or upgrade-glue-lake-formation exactly. A claim 'Lake Formation permissions replace IAM' is wrong as written: the pages describe both layers.

Data filters (d043): column-level, row-level and cell-level security are separate capabilities with limitations per engine (data-filtering-notes, athena-lf, emr-integ-lf, qs-integ-lf); keep the engine in the claim.

EMR single AZ (d047): 'a cluster runs in one Availability Zone' needs the sentence (FAQ 45 or emr-plan-vpc-subnet). Multiple primary nodes do not protect against an AZ failure: quote the considerations page if it says so; do not infer it.

EMR Spot (d049): the guidance is that task nodes suit Spot and the primary and core nodes of long-running clusters should be On-Demand; quote the guideline sentences, with the cluster type (long-running vs transient) as written.
HDFS vs EMRFS (d048): 'HDFS data is lost when the cluster terminates' needs the ephemeral sentence of emr-plan-file-systems as written.

OpenSearch, Quick and Data Exchange are recognise-only service cards: 6 to 10 facts each, the ones a question or a card would use (what it is, the deciding feature, one security and one resilience fact). Do not mine every feature.
Quick naming: quote the what-is page for 'Amazon Quick' and 'Quick Sight'; the 'formerly QuickSight' link is a change fact (numbers lens, d022).

Decision guide and whitepapers (d055, d056): quote whole table rows or whole sentences; the big-data whitepaper is older (it may say Elasticsearch or QuickSight): keep the quote, note the current name in the claim, and prefer the guide page when both say the same thing.

Callvale story values (two years of JSON transcripts, 9 seconds today, under 1 second target, personal-data columns) are story data, never facts; d060 lists the AWS facts each reason cites. The story never teaches a fact; a sub-second search latency claim for OpenSearch needs a page sentence or the claim is narrowed to 'search' without a number.
Case studies: only the ten usable ones; quotes at most 25 words.

faq.job: Quick-fire FAQ facts for the FAQ section (verbatim FAQ answers, one or two sentences each): the questions listed in d062 (Athena), d063 (Glue), d064 (Lake Formation), d065 (EMR), d066 (OpenSearch Service), d067 (Amazon Quick) and d068 (Data Exchange). Each fact quotes the answer sentence(s) whole; the claim keeps the answer's conditions. Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, decision, limit.
watch: The FAQ lists (work files faq-*.txt) give the question numbers used in the demand items; the last item of each list is an empty 'NA' entry, skip it. Athena item 1 '[Machine learning] Machine Learning' is a section label, not a question.

FAQ answers can be older than the guide (for example QuickSight-era wording, Elasticsearch names, Kinesis Data Analytics in Glue FAQ 28, old Glue billing minimums): when a FAQ statement disagrees with the guide, quotas or pricing page, let the numbers or behavior lens add the guide value, record the conflict in the demand note and do not add the FAQ statement as a competing fact.

Before adding a FAQ fact for something the other lenses cover (pricing, comparisons), check `facts list --service <key>`; the FAQ lens adds the quick-fire sentence only when it states something new or states it in the form the FAQ section quotes.
Glue FAQ 28 compares Glue Streaming with Kinesis Data Analytics (fully shut down 2026-01-27): skip it.

rules: Quote from page snapshots only; full.md hits are pointers.
A demand item becomes filled, contradicted (with what the page says) or not-found.
Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only.
Files of 10 to 25 facts; every quote verbatim and complete for its claim; `--by mine-35-<lens>`.
Never refresh a cached page; fetch only a page that is not yet in the corpus.
